core.title: No file extensions in component URNs; use a language facet
core.given: A component URN is involved, in any artifact
core.when: choosing or checking the segment of the component URN that names the component, especially when a language needs to be shown
core.then: Never put a file extension in a component URN; if a language must be expressed, use the URN's language facet.
avoid: A component URN whose name segment ends in a file extension, e.g. naming the component after its source file with the suffix included.
core.why: The URN names a logical component, not a file.
evidence: No component URN contains a file extension of any kind.
verification: Scope: every component URN in any artifact, whether new, edited, copied or referenced. The name segment must contain no file extension of any kind; the prohibition is general and not limited to an enumerated list of suffixes.
Expressing a language through the URN's language facet waives nothing: the URN must still satisfy the stack's canonical component URN shape and its casing rules.

Detector coverage: the finding 'component URN contains a file extension' has no existing observer; a repository-wide check needs a detector that recognizes file extensions inside component URN strings (activation observability: needs_new_observer).

values: component URN contains a file extension

fires: A component URN appears in any artifact, whether new, edited, copied or referenced.
A component's language needs to be expressed in its URN.

profileRequirements.meaning: The component URN shape: segment order (which segment names the component), separators and facet syntax, including how a language is expressed as a facet. The core refers to 'the name segment' and 'the language facet' and requires the URN to still match this shape; the literal facet spelling and the canonical regex live here, not in the core.
profileRequirements.bunValue: component:{wagon}:{feature}:{name}:{side}:{layer} with '.' as facet separator; a language is expressed as a 'lang-*' facet in the name segment; must match the canonical lint regex ^component:[a-z][a-z0-9-]*:[a-z][a-z0-9-]*:[a-zA-Z0-9.]+:(frontend|backend|fe|be):(presentation|application|domain|integration|assembly)$ (bun.json's counter-example component:resolve-dilemmas:choose-option:OptionValidator.py:backend:domain instantiates the shape)

bunOnly.text: Never put a file extension (.py, .dart, .ts, .tsx, etc.) in a component URN. If a language must be expressed, use a 'lang-*' facet.
bunOnly.reason: Enumerates concrete languages' file suffixes and spells the stack's literal facet syntax ('lang-*'); the neutral core forbids any file extension and defers facet syntax to the profile key urn.component.
A concrete counter-example URN from the Bun repository, including a .py suffix; bun.json itself is delivered as the reference example, so the concrete URN is not repeated in the core.

bunOnly.reason: The enumerated suffix list names specific languages; the neutral evidence keeps only the general 'file extension of any kind' form.

bunOnly.text: Forbidden: .py, .dart, .ts, .tsx. The source says 'etc.', so other file extensions are forbidden too.
bunOnly.reason: The detector's concrete match set enumerates language-specific suffixes; the neutral check (core.verification) forbids any file extension, which is what 'etc.' already generalizes to.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is fully neutral: a component URN names a logical component, so its name segment must never carry a file extension of any kind (Bun's 'etc.' already generalizes past the enumerated list, so dropping the enumeration neither weakens nor strengthens the rule). What could not be neutralized: the illustrative enumeration of concrete file suffixes (.py, .dart, .ts, .tsx), the literal 'lang-*' facet spelling, the canonical lint regex, and the cross-reference to the sibling casing rule planner.component.urn.casing — these stay in the Bun realization (bunOnly) or in the profile via urn.component. The core speaks of 'the URN's language facet'; each stack supplies its concrete facet syntax and URN shape through urn.component, so no proposedKeys were needed. core.verification records the needs_new_observer limitation exactly as bun.json does and adds no interim enforcement disposition.
